A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Flow Matching for Tabular Data Synthesis. All 27 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–E report original experiments comparing synthesis methods, trajectories, integration settings and stochastic sampling.

after.justification: Retains original experimental results and adds fidelity evaluations, high-cardinality and high-dimensional stress tests, and backbone comparisons in Appendices E and G.

M1.justification: The core TabSynFlow and TabbyFlow procedures remain. Appendix G.2.2 adds a 256-dimensional projection with layer normalisation before the VAE for gene-expression synthesis, and G.3 evaluates a Transformer backbone for TabbyFlow. These are local architectural adaptations.

E1.justification: Appendix G.2 adds Diabetes and Gene Expression of Cancer, extending coverage to healthcare and genomics under high categorical cardinality and 20,264 numerical dimensions. Indonesia, Adult and Churn were already evaluated in v1; their appearance in the main text is a relocation.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain TabDDPM, TabSyn and the four OT/VP flow variants, including v1 Table 9 versus v2 Table 3. The added diagnostic comparisons use the same methods; new citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Adds WD, MMD, Shape, Trend, C2ST, alpha-precision and beta-recall evaluation, including 5,000-record batches and a held-out classifier test. Stress tests introduce feature exclusions, dimensionality reduction and a two-component utility score for gene expression. Original training and sampling defaults remain.

E4.justification: New stress tests examine latent-space versus data-space synthesis under extreme cardinality and dimensionality, while Appendix G.3 tests MLP versus Transformer backbones across the original datasets. Earlier variance, interpolant, integration and stochastic-sampling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports plus/minus values. v2 newly specifies 20 synthetic-generation seeds and identifies these values as one standard deviation, without establishing an increase in runs or repeated training. Tables 9 and 13 nevertheless omit deviations despite their captions promising them.

E6.justification: Indonesia TabbyFlow-OT utility changes from 0.6671 to 0.9191 and risk from 0.4114 to 0.6556, changing the utility winner from TabSynFlow-OT to TabbyFlow-OT (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 3). Related Indonesia results and NFE curves are revised. Numerous diagnostic and stress-test results are added; the cause of the Indonesia revisions is unstated.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 2.6 drops the negative sign present in v1 Equation 2.8, introducing an incorrect KL-to-log-likelihood equality. Appendix F.1 corrects the Gaussian interpolant description from marginal to conditional, and D.3 adds diagnostic definitions. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, research questions and listed contributions retain their meaning. The conclusion preserves the central utility and efficiency claims, OT recommendation, VP risk trade-off and dataset-dependent benefits of stochastic sampling.

C2.justification: Adds interpretations concerning fidelity versus coverage, representation suitability and backbone capacity in Appendices E.1 and G.2–G.3. The broader-impact statement adds rare-group bias and residual disclosure concerns. Some new interpretations conflict with evidence, notably the Diabetes discussion claiming lower WD for TabSynFlow despite Table 23.

D1.justification: Newly documents Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.3.0 and an L40S GPU, provides access references and preprocessing details for the stress-test datasets, and clarifies backbone implementation choices. Most original architecture, training-budget and sampling details were already supplied.

R1.justification: Adds Adams et al. on fidelity/privacy, Gat et al. on discrete FM, Jolicoeur-Martineau et al. on tree-based generation, and evaluation references by Little and Taub; removes Tong et al. The principal positioning relative to TabSyn and prior TabbyFlow remains.

P1.justification: Moves trajectory and TabSyn background into appendices, subdivides and expands Section 4, rewrites the main comparison and conclusion, and reorganises the appendices around diagnostics and ablations. A broader-impact statement replaces the acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Adds seven diagnostic tables and three stress-test/backbone tables, expands Table 1 with categorical-cardinality columns, and redraws Figure 1 with a risk zoom panel and revised caption. The earlier additional-dataset table moves into the main text, and Figure 5 corrects the TabVFM legend to TabbyFlow.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful fidelity, scalability and backbone evidence and clarifies reproducibility information. However, it introduces the Equation 2.6 sign error, conflicting C2ST definitions and interpretations, and Diabetes claims inconsistent with Table 23. Table 19 also retains obsolete averages after revising Indonesia: its OT utility average remains 0.7565 although the displayed rows average 0.7925. These benefits and reliability problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
